title: ROAD CLOSED
full_story:
The City of Flora will be closing Charlie Brown Park on Thursday and reopening on Friday afternoon due to tilling, shaping and sealing of the roads.

Campers will be able to access rear entrance to campsites only the rest of park will be closed.  Golfers please use the Country Club’s west entrance off of Country Club Road during these times as the east entrance will be blocked off.  The City apologizes for the inconvenience.  There will be temporary intermittent closures across town these two days as well for some spot patching and oiling as well.

title: CLAY COUNTY BOARD
full_story:
Board members approved the $15,335,778 proposed budget to cover the county’s tax levies.  This will be available for the public to view for the next 30 days.

Board members heard from Dave Stryker and Erica Glenn, Senior Manager, Development of Key Capture Energy.  The company is a battery energy storage company, from Houston, Texas.  “The 10-acre battery storage facility will be connected directly to the Ameren substation,” Glenn explained.  “We have been working on this project since 2021, directly with Ameren.  The money for decommissioning and road agreement means if the company goes bankrupt or has other issues, we would be responsible for removing everything.  We are not connected to the data center nor to the solar farm.  There are 14 substations in Texas and New York.”  “We are good neighbors for road maintenance and will work with local fire departments for training.  We will bring in $500,000 tax revenue a year.”

The Xenia Substation will be located on 10 acres of land owned by Scott Suntrup, on Cypress Drive.  They hope to start construction in the next 12 to 18 months.  The energy company has a life span of 20 to 30 years.  One of the board members asked about fire safety and Glenn explained they would be covered by the Ameren substation.  Board members Terry Hronac asked about impact on ground water, which he was guaranteed there would be no issue.  Board Chairman Joe Goodman asked for a vote from the board, as long as all the Xs were covered.  All board members approved the motion.

Clay County Hospital CEO/President Bob Sellers received approval for staff credentials, the purchase of a Hematology Analyzer for $34,875; an IT Server replacement for $270,011.22 and a Convoltherm Combi Oven Maxx Pro for $20,205.19.  Sellers reported the hospital extension steel package will start in November.  Plumbing and electrical is ready, and gravel is being laid for concert to be poured.  The hospital received a Rural Health Transformational Grant for $356,000.

Lyn Waller presented the Clay County Health Department report.  Beyond the Bell currently has 97 youth enrolled, with a fiscal-year average daily attendance of 48.  As of September 22, 70.1% percent of enrolled youth were ages 11–17, meeting the Teen REACH requirement of 70%.  Younger youth continue to be waitlisted as needed to maintain the required age distribution.

Beyond the Bell will host its annual Lights on Afterschool Open House on October 22nd.  Dinner will be offered from 3 to 4 pm followed by activities from 4 to 6 pm.  Families, community partners, and community members are invited to visit the program and learn more about available opportunities for youth.

Approximately 93-94% of individuals who contracted measles in 2025 and 2026 were completely unvaccinated or had and unknown vaccination history.  Measles vaccination remains the best way to prevent measles and to stop the outbreak.  The vaccine offers 97% protection against the measles virus for those receiving the recommended two-dose series.  Kindergarten exemption rates have reached record highs in multiple states causing concerns for many more cases to occur.  Nine Illinois counties have fallen below the 95% threshold required for community herd immunity for the current school year.  Illinois has 22 cases confirmed so far in 2026.  Please call to schedule or stop by to have their professional staff provide you with that vaccination anytime.

All vaccinations are available to the public daily.  The department has begun offering influenza and Covid-19 vaccines through the drive-thru vaccine clinics on Wednesdays.  The vaccines will also be available all other days of the week and can be brought out to vehicles by calling the Health Department phone line and letting staff know the need.  Multiple clinics have been set up for onsite influenza vaccinations at a variety of locations during this season.  Please check The Clay County Health Department website for locations and times of availability.

Sheriff Andy Myers presented the sheriff’s office September report.  The board approved purchasing Axon Enterprise 60 lease for body cam/in car/taser.

Circuit Clerk Crystall Ballard report was approved amending the resolution establishing of Civil Fees and Criminal Traffic assessments.  State statute fee changed by $20.

County Engineer Darin Koelm presented the engineer’s report.  Koelm stated they are continuing mowing and preparing for the upcoming winter.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens received approval for the yearly Appellate Prosecutor’s Office resolution and a resolution for County Board Chairman Joe Goodman to vote in county board meetings.  “I have always voted during meetings,” Chairman Goodman explained.  “I was voted to the board to represent my district, and my chairman appointment was made by board members.”

In Executive finance report, board member Terry Hronec received approval to purchase K-9 equipment for the Sheriff department vehicle at $11,899, Capital Expenditure funds; replacement of Net Gear switch in the Supervisor of Assessments Office, at $1,753.30, to be paid from Capital Expenditure funds.

The Hope Trust 2027 premium increase was approved split 50/50 between the county and employees.

The board approved re-appointment of Brandi Young to the 708 board, for a 4-year term.

Clay County Sheriff’s Office September activity report includes issuing 12 traffic citations, 30 criminal arrests, 38 various civil papers, 24 criminal and 12 accident investigations.  The Sheriff’s Office received $981.70 which included: $582 civil process; $8 E-citations; $91.70 IDOC transport fees and $300 bonds.

Board member Janice Brooks presented the claims report as follows; $4,467,401.18 Hospital paid claims and $453,312.69 unpaid claims; $44,325.50 County Highway paid claims and $376.20 unpaid claims; $389,422.78 Health Department paid claims and $109,638.48 unpaid claims; $186,797.47 Clay County paid claims and no unpaid claims; $81,924.12 – 911 paid claims and no unpaid claims; $56,949.16 Public Safety Tax paid claims and no unpaid claims; $4,389.36 Animal Control paid claims and no unpaid claims.

title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board met Tuesday evening and acted on a variety of items on a busy agenda.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order and trustees made quick order of approving the past meeting minutes and the bills, before welcoming a visitor, Clark Cameron with the Illinois Rural Water Association.  Cameron was on hand to give the results on a rate study conducted for the village.  The Clay City water fund is not self-sustaining, and he was looking at how they could make improvements to become so.  He said village rates are at the low end of what other villages of comparable sizes charge.  He added that local governments should view and operate the utility as a business and not lose money.  He believes the village should have no problem in becoming self-sustaining and could easily implement a one-dollar rate increase or more if needed.  Trustees then began a conversation about increasing village water rates but took no action and will discuss their options at the November meeting.

The mayor turned to the topic of making repairs to the sewer lagoon.  One side of the lagoon was never completed and it is a concern.  Members discussed the need to bring in clay and top it with riprap to prevent erosion.  An earlier bid to do the work has expired and trustees worried about the associated costs but realize it needs to be completed.  In the end, members voted to seek two bids…one that includes the work and the cost of riprap and the other for the work alone, as the village may purchase its own materials.

Mayor Delonshaw also brought up the earlier topic of purchasing an extended warranty for its backhoe.  Two options were presented, 24 and 36 months.  Members chose the latter which includes up to 1,500 hours at a cost of $5,016.  They had also discussed financing the purchase price of $52,494, but balked when the finance charges came to over $13,000 and they decided not to finance it.

Village Attorney Barry Bright brought the board back to the topic of setting the village tax levy.  With the village trying to shore up its water fund and the general fund, he suggested the most appropriate manner of accomplishing the task.  First, the village could pass the typical annual increase of 4.99%, which would add roughly $4,174 to village coffers.  The board could then also increase another utility to help make up the amount it needs.  After considering a few options, trustees opted to increase the monthly trash fee by $5 per account, to $19 per month, still well below what other communities charge.  Bright also stated that following the action taken in September to set a standard utility deposit, the board needed to codify that action and approve the ordinance officially setting the fee at $700.  Members approved the measure unanimously.

Utility Superintendent Sean Sullens brought up the need to purchase a snow plow for the village’s newly purchased truck.  He had quotes from two vendors, one from Olney and one from Danville.  Trustees approved purchasing from the Olney business, BM Truck Equipment at a cost of $12,501.  Sullens also requested to purchase metal siding to repair the Clark addition pump house at a cost of $716 from Zink Building Center and board consensus was to agree to allow for the repair to be completed.

Before the meeting drew to a close the board approved setting a special meeting on November 2nd at 4:00pm to discuss personnel issues and to review closed session minutes.

Trustees then turned to the topic of reviewing monthly cash balances and transfers report.  Members went through confidential utility past due amounts and discussed options of how to collect on past due amounts or turning off customers utilities for non-payment.  Members also discussed how to rid the village of nuisance properties and contemplated taking action to force compliance or perhaps even purchasing properties and demolishing dilapidated homes that are now nothing more than an eyesore.  Any action to be taken remains to be seen.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
Louisville trustees met Tuesday evening, taking care of some of the last few months of 2026 business.

The agenda was passed as well as minutes from September 21st and two October 1st special meetings.  Trustees approved September bills.  A $500,000 CD purchase was also approved.

After a long discussion, trustees approved sidewalk bid for $30,000 for approximately 843 feet of sidewalk replacement.  The bid was awarded to Rusty Harper.  They agreed that some sidewalks should be five foot wide and others four foot wide.  Those designated for five-foot-wide sidewalks include areas on Kinmundy Road, Chestnut, Broadway and on Route 45.  The agreement will include village employees removing the old sidewalks.

Christmas decorations were discussed and electric lines will be moved to take care of problems on Chestnut Street.

A façade grant was awarded to Doug Harrison for Harrison Insurance, 230 Route 45 South.

Trustees tabled the final design of the murals on the village square until Mayor Chris Rinehart meets with the painter/designer.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
Village Superintendent Travis Lewis shared a message from Engineer Brandon Bridges with Charleston Engineering that if the village needed to bring in and excavation team for the planned road repairs the work would be delayed Six months to a year to allow for soil testing or the village could handle the digging to avoid delaying the project.

In village business, Xenia Village Police Chief Jerry Burkett gave Trustees an update on the state

of properties in the village.  “ Some people are still doing clean up and some are still making

messes.  I expect things will slow down as winter approaches; But we have defiantly showed residents we mean business issuing citation violations” he told trustees.  Burkett then addressed police business in the village.  He informed trustees that one of the two upgraded mobile data centers for the villages police vehicles had been installed in the cruiser.  He is also awaiting upgrade and installation of the second unit by Flora Police.

Village Superintendent Travis Lewis informed village trustees that he and his crew were addressing duck weed growth near the villages lift station.

Trustees also discussed amending three ordinances within the village.  The first is an amendment to the villages solicitation ordinance restricting solicitation hours to daylight hour or out right banning solicitation with in the village.  The ban if possible would exclude not for profit and charity fundraising sales.  “I get roughly two calls a week from residents informing me that someone is knocking on their door in the middle of the night; these solicitors are also pushy and often not carrying a valid form of I.D. that can be processed by our computer systems allowing me to cite them.  It’s a situation that could escalate and end badly” Burkett told trustees.

Trustees discussed adding an ordinance that disallows camping and fires on village property.  Highlighting a recent interaction, he had with a homeless individual who attempted to set up camp next to the village pond.  Burkett told trustees “addition of this kind of ordinance is necessary as we see an increase in homelessness in the area.”

Trustee’s then discussed amending the ordinance on trustee attendance of village board meeting and payment.  These issues were tabled pending further research on how to proceed.

Trustees discussed the upcoming election in December.  This included which trustees’ seats would need to be vacated and when, as well as what steps trustees need to take for reelection.

The Villages Trunk or Treat will be held on October 24th from 5 to 8 pm.  The Village is planning a Breakfast fundraiser for November 21st from 6 to 11 am.

The next Xenia Village board meeting will be on December 8th at 5:30 pm.

title: POOLE TO BE INDUCTED
full_story:
The National Athletic Hall of Fame Selection Committee will induct Randy Poole in the Media – Sports Broadcaster category Friday evening at the Teutopolis Banquet Hall in Teutopolis.

For more than three decades, Randy was one of the most recognizable voices in regional athletics.  He served as the longtime broadcaster for Flora Wolves football (34 years) and Flora Wolves basketball (15 years) on WNOI, becoming a trusted and familiar presence for generations of athletes, families, and fans.  In addition to his play-by-play work, Poole also spent 15 years as Sports Director, covering football, basketball, baseball, softball, and junior high athletics throughout the region.

Randy’s dedication extends far beyond the broadcast booth.  He has been an active member of the Flora Rotary Club for 30 years, served on the Flora Academic Foundation Board and the Flora Chamber of Commerce, and remains a committed member of the First Methodist Church in Flora, where he serves on the Church Council.

The 2026 Induction Ceremony will again be held on Friday evening at the Teutopolis Banquet Hall in Teutopolis.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Clay County Sheriff Andy Myers issued his monthly activity report during Tuesday’s Clay County Board meeting.  In the Report for September, the Sheriff’s Office issued a total of 12 Traffic Citations, made 30 Criminal Arrests and served 38 various Civil Papers.  A total of 21,535 miles were driven by Sheriff’s personnel during the month.

24 persons were processed through the Clay County Jail during September.  There were 4 inmates in jail at the beginning of the month and 8 in jail at the end of the month.  The average daily jail population was 8.

Also, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office received a total of $982 during the month.  This includes:

The Sheriff’s Office handled approximately 344 complaints, 75 of which originated in Louisville and 77 in Clay City.  The Sheriff’s Office conducted 24 Criminal Investigations and 12 Accident Investigations during September.
